v.title: Nations League Quarter-Final Draw: When, Where, and What It Means for Barça
v.excerpt: Nations League quarter‑final draw set for June 26: Barça’s European future could hinge on the matchups revealed tonight.
v.body:
## Quick take
The Nations League quarter‑final draw will take place on Thursday, 26 June, at 20:00 GMT in Brussels. All 16 teams are set to be paired, and the draw will determine who faces who in the last 16 of the competition.

## What happened
BBC’s Ask Me Anything team broke down the schedule, confirming that the draw is slated for the evening of 26 June. It will be conducted live on the BBC’s streaming platform, with representatives from all participating national teams in attendance. The event is slated to run for roughly 30 minutes, after which the first round of quarter‑final fixtures will be revealed.

The Nations League, organised by UEFA, is now in its final stages. Sixteen teams remain, having progressed from the group phase. The draw will decide the matchups for the last 16, with the winners advancing to the semi‑finals. This marks a crucial juncture for all clubs, as the competition offers a guaranteed spot in the Champions League for the winners.

## Why it matters
- **Barcelona’s European ambitions**: A Nations League win guarantees Barça a Champions League berth, sidestepping the need to finish high enough in La Liga. With the squad still recovering from a congested schedule, a smooth route into Europe could free up resources for the domestic campaign.
- **Player morale and rhythm**: The draw will set the stage for key players like Pedri and Gavi to face either top‑tier or mid‑table opposition. The level of challenge will influence their match fitness and confidence heading into the second half of the season.
- **Managerial strategy**: Ronald Koeman’s squad will need to balance the Nations League with the Europa League and domestic fixtures. Knowing the draw early allows him to plan rotation, ensuring he can field a competitive lineup while keeping the squad fresh for La Liga’s decisive matches.

## What’s next
Watch the live draw on 26 June at 20:00 GMT. Pay special attention to the pairings involving Spain and Portugal, as these matchups will test Barcelona’s depth against top‑flight opposition. The outcomes will dictate the fixture calendar for the next month, affecting training schedules and injury management. Keep an eye on the BBC stream for real‑time commentary and expert analysis—this is the moment that could shape Barça’s European destiny.
